**Reasoning:**
The white cottony mycelial growth concentrated at the stem/soil interface is the hallmark sign of **Southern Blight** caused by *Sclerotium rolfsii*. This pathogen produces dense white mycelium at and below the soil line, with associated crown/stem rot. Sclerotinia Timber Rot can look similar but typically affects higher stem sections and produces large black sclerotia internally. The location (soil level), the dense white fluffy mycelium spreading from the crown, and the pattern of infection all point strongly to Southern Blight.
